messages:
emily: Hey team — got a customer escalation: p95 up ~3x and p99 spikes after last runtime rollout (v3.2.1). Customer saw it start ~12:05 UTC. Their traffic is standard chat gen, ~2k reqs/min.
jun: Can you paste the customer request IDs or tenant id? any correlation to model/sequence-length? :eyes:
emily: Tenant: acme-inc, sample requests here: reqs/abcd1234..abcd1240. Mostly seq len 512, no unusual prompt patterns.
oncall-bot: Deploy bot: rollout v3.2.1 -> v3.2.1 completed at 11:58:43 UTC to 100% (canary passed).
alex: Interesting — deploy finished ~12:00 then p95 jumped at 12:05. Are we sure it was full rollout and not a variant swap?
maria: Checking metrics now — opening dashboard. p95 heatmap shows cluster subset with tail. Link: https://grafana/redwood/d/latency/rollout (shared)
nate: I see host group rtx-43 showing long tail and elevated heap growth. p99 aligns with GC pause events in logs.
jun: GC pauses? v3.2.1 bumped jemalloc/allocator flags and default batch size, right? That could increase allocation churn for certain workloads.
emily: Correct — release notes: "allocator: aggressive coalescing and batch_size=256 by default". We rolled that flag in.
alex: Quick repro: curl customer endpoint with seq=512 payload, run a loop to flood at 50 rps, capture /debug/alloc-snapshot and /metrics. Use this command: 
```
for i in 1..200; do curl -sS -H "x-tenant: acme-inc" -d @payload.json https://api.redwood/v1/generate; done
```
Collect /metrics from the host.
maria: Running synthetic against canary pool shows p95 elevated only when request rate spikes above 40 RPS and when sequence length >400. At low rps it's fine.
nate: Hypothesis: allocator change + higher batch size increases per-request memory working set -> GC stutter under load. That causes tail at p95/p99.
jun: Agreed. Proposed mitigations: 1) roll back allocator flag (flip to legacy) in runtime config for affected hosts, 2) temporarily reduce batch_size to 64 for acme-inc route, 3) route acme-inc to v3.1.9 variant while we bisect.
emily: Support has SLA window — customer needs mitigation now, can we do a quick variant route?
support: I can open a routing override for acme-inc to v3.1.9 and throttle burst. Will do if ops approves.
alex: Ops: to be safe, do a partial rollback on the subset of rtx-43 hosts hitting the tail. Steps: 
- run config flip: `fleetctl set runtime.alloc_policy=legacy --selector=pool=rtx-43`
- decrease runtime.batch_size=64 for route acme-inc
- monitor p95 for 15m
If p95 improves, plan full rollback or staged kernel/alloc tuning.
maria: Setting up a short synthetic replay against rtx-43 to validate before customer action. ETA 5m.
oncall-bot: Note: I'm creating incident INC-2026 for this escalation and paging oncall.
emily: Thanks. I'll notify customer that we're investigating and performing temporary routing change.
jun: After mitigation, we should bisect the allocator change: run a controlled A/B with binary search on the allocator patch range (commit 9a3..e2f). Put 50% traffic on legacy, 50% on new for a small cohort and capture alloc traces + GC logs.
nate: I'll prepare the bisection harness and alloc heap snapshots. Need to ensure we have sampling enabled: `runtime.debug.alloc_sampling=1` on test cohort.
alex: Also add a synthetic test to our CI that mimics seq=512 chat traffic to catch regressions going forward.
maria: Update: routing override applied to acme-inc -> v3.1.9. Preliminary p95 dropped back near baseline within 4 minutes.
support: Customer updated: they see improvement, monitoring closely, appreciate quick action. :thumbsup:
emily: Good. Next steps: run binary bisect across allocator commits, evaluate whether to tune flags (lower batch_size globally vs revert change), and add guard in rollout (trial with heavy-chat cohort). I'll own the follow-up doc and postmortem.
jun: I'll run bisect today and loop in research for allocator tuning. If we confirm allocator root cause, we can release a hotfix with safer defaults.
alex: Add a runbook snippet to incidents doc: quick mitigation steps and exact fleetctl commands.
maria: small nit: we should also add telemetry alert for heap growth correlation with p95 so this gets auto-detected next time.
emily: Awesome, closing thread for now — thanks all. We'll update INC-2026 with notes and timeline.
